_comment: REWARD-ECONOMY (prompt 58). The chapter's reward audit, as data. One row per activity that pays something, in route order, recording what it gives, what that lets the player DO next, and whether the player can be expected to understand that use at the moment they receive it -- which is prompt 58's actual test ('a reward is good when the player can connect it to something they want to do next'), not whether a prize exists. Rewards themselves live where they always have: trainer payouts in the band trainer files, shop stock in trade.json, recipes in data/recipes/, world pickups in playground_world.gd. Nothing here is a second economy; this is the map of the one that ships, and tests/test_chapter_rewards.gd checks the map against it.
_comment_no_new_systems: Prompt 58 opens by forbidding a second inventory, currency, recipe or loot system, so this file deliberately holds no numbers the game reads. It is an audit and a set of invariants. The one CHANGE the audit produced was a placement, not a system: three apex TMs (tm_earthshatter/tm_leviathan_surge/tm_heavenfall) existed as items with full move data and no acquisition path anywhere in the game -- see playground_world.gd's TM_AT.

materials._comment: Prompt 58's resource tiers, with the use that makes each one worth picking up. Audited 2026-08-22: every material the world can yield is a recipe input, a build cost or shop stock -- there are no orphan collectibles in the Meadows.
materials._comment_supply: Measured against data/config/bands/*/harvest.json plus the warrens deposits: rootstone supply 28 against 12 needed by the two critical-path recipes (Riding Saddle 8, Greater Orb 4); ironwood 15 against orb_prime's 4. Both comfortable, neither so loose the material stops mattering.

activities.enables: First coins and the first potion — the potion teaches that damage is recoverable outside a menu.
Coins toward Mira's own store, which she keeps — the one trainer whose reward and whose sink are the same person.
Three Basic Orbs, immediately after Tam teaches the orb recipe. This is the chapter's clearest reward-to-use link: the thing he explains and the thing he hands over are the same thing.
The South Bridge Key — the reward IS the progression. Opens Band 2.
Coins and potions before the quarry and the warrens, the longest stretch so far without a bed.
activities.note: Optional. Sited so the player meets it needing exactly what it pays.

activities.enables: Three Basic Orbs at the door of the dungeon whose field is the strongest the player has met — the means to catch what is behind him.
activities.note: Optional. Prompt 58's 'optional trainers need enough value to justify engagement'.

activities.enables: Plus 4 rootstone and 1 stone from the cave's own wall deposits. Two Greater Orbs the moment the branch door goes down, with the vault's Elder Trailpup standing behind it; rootstone for the saddle and the Greater Orb recipe; the Heartstone that gates the chapter's one evolution (Mudsnout -> Tuskroot); and a Hide Vest, the guardian's own armor and the first equipment reward in the chapter.
activities.note: CONTENT-0828, owner playtest 2026-08-28 ("there needs to be a point to going in the burrows warren"). This row is where that complaint shows up as a number. The old payout was 45 coins, 4 rootstone and 60 xp — the chapter's ONE REQUIRED DUNGEON, five resident fights and a level-14 guardian at a measured 5-9 minutes, paying LESS than Pell, the optional picket standing 35 m outside its own door (40 coins, 2 potions, 3 orbs), and under a third of relay_captain Vance one band later. A boss that pays picket money is a boss with no point. Same reward SHAPE as every other row here — no second economy, per this file's own _comment_no_new_systems — at boss scale. The Greater Orbs are the deliberate part and they follow this region's own established logic: trainers.json says Pell pays BASIC orbs because "the reward for clearing the door is the means to catch what is behind it", so the guardian pays GREATER orbs because what is behind HIM, through the door his defeat just opened, is the vault's Elder Trailpup (burrow_warrens.json _comment_spawns_special) at level 13. The Heartstone's use is legible at the moment it is taken — BAND2-63-WARRENS put the evolution lead into the pickup line itself — which is what flips understood_when_received; the earlier false predates that change. T3-REWARD added hide_vest per owner-direction §14 ('Warrens Guardian: Rootstone progression + useful TM/equipment/recipe'); armor had no acquisition path anywhere in the game before this. UPDATED: the FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD fix that landed on main 2026-08-29 replaced the vault's wild Terrapup with an Elder Trailpup -- Terrapup is one of three starter species and cannot be an ordinary catchable wild (see tests/test_spawns_data.gd's STARTER_SPECIES) -- so this row's own species reference was stale against burrow_warrens.json until this edit; nothing about the reward shape, level or orb tier changed.

activities.enables: Coins and a potion on the relay approach.
Coins and potions, escalating with the rank.
Two Greater Orbs — the first time the better orb tier arrives as a reward rather than a recipe, and the region's wild band is high enough that the difference is felt.
The Mill Bridge Gear (progression), a Revive, three Greater Orbs and the chapter's first xp_bonus. The largest single payout before the finale.

River Sigil (progression) plus Greater Orbs and a permanent HP elixir — owner-direction §14's 'Captain 3: Sigil + final preparation unlock/reward', added by T3-REWARD. Riverwatch is the last of the three Sigils, so this is the last thing the ladder hands over before the Meadows Hall gate opens.

Field Sigil (progression), potions, and a strong Ground TM — owner-direction §14's 'Captain 1: Sigil + strong TM', added by T3-REWARD. Was previously the one captain reward with no TM in it; every existing Ground TM came from a world pickup or Mira's shop, never a fight.
Ridge Sigil (progression), a Revive, and a permanent defence elixir — owner-direction §14's 'Captain 2: Sigil + equipment/preparation improvement', added by T3-REWARD.
The gauntlet's coins arrive too late for Mira's store to matter, so these are consumables for the Warden fight specifically — which is the correct shape for a reward paid inside the final building.
The chapter's largest xp_bonus, revives and potions.

activities.activity: TM: Stone Rush / Burrow Strike (world pickups)
activities.enables: Two Ground TMs in the opening field — team-building choice from the first hour.

activities.activity: TM: Earthshatter / Leviathan Surge / Heavenfall (world pickups)
activities.enables: One apex TM per type (power 2.0, the highest in data/moves/moves.json), each off-spine in the late region that owns its type. The reward for choosing to explore instead of walking the road.
activities.note: ADDED by this audit. All three shipped as items with full move and compatibility data and no way to obtain them; see playground_world.gd's TM_AT.

activities.enables: Nine TMs at 120-300 coins, orbs, potions, revives and seeds — the chapter's coin sink. Total coin income from required and optional trainers is 860 plus 30 starting, so a player who fights everything can afford roughly three of the expensive TMs: a real choice, not a shopping list.
Pays the entry back and restocks the potions the three rounds will spend. The quarter is the round a player can lose and retry, so its reward has to survive being earned late.
Orbs, deliberately: the tournament is the last beat before South Bridge, and the leg past it is where a team gets its fourth and fifth creature.

The chapter's transition prize. Coins and potions restock for the road; `recipe_saddle` is the real reward and the 2026-08-22 owner directive's own wording -- 'winning grants the saddle recipe, and an NPC line tells the player the mount species can be ridden'. It is the one recipe in recipes_rootstone.json carrying an unlock flag, because a prize the player already has is not a prize.

The chapter's baseline income and the reason to fight something you are not catching. XP is split across everyone who fought (party_share 0.5), so an ordinary fight pays the whole team -- which is what makes a five-creature roster raisable at all.

invariants._comment: What tests/test_chapter_rewards.gd fails the build over. Each is one of prompt 58's own acceptance bullets turned into something checkable.
invariants._comment_coins: Two rather than three so ordinary play, not completionist play, clears the bar.

_comment_audit_gap_closed: The four rows above were missing when the 2026-08-22 Gate C audit read this file against prompt 58, which names 'Tournament: coins/reward/status that makes victory feel meaningful and transitions the chapter' and 'ordinary wild fights' as required sections of the reward map. The REWARDS existed -- data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json has paid all three tournament rounds since TOURNAMENT-1 -- but an audit table that omits the chapter's transition prize cannot answer the question it exists to answer. Read off the shipping data, not invented: coins 20/25/40, potions 2/-/3, orbs -/3/-, and recipe_saddle on the final's own reward.flags.
